title: Introduce proportional failure heatmap and context coverage CI hook
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Add a new CI hook that computes a proportional failure heatmap and context-coverage score per prompt cohort. Soft-fail mode by default; opt-in hard gating available via project config. Adds dashboard panels and backfill script.
description: Motivation: some regressions surface only in high-volume contexts or in narrow prompt cohorts; existing eval gates treat each failing example equally which underweights production impact. This PR introduces a proportional failure heatmap and a context-coverage metric that (1) weights failures by frequency and severity, (2) surfaces top-left hotspots in a time-decayed heatmap, and (3) produces a single coverage score used by the CI hook. Design: we cluster prompts into contextual cohorts using the existing prompt fingerprinting + semantic shingle embedding. For each cohort we compute a weighted failure score = sum_{examples in cohort}(failure_weight * recency_decay * frequency_factor). Frequency comes from the sampled traffic histogram (or sample proxy during CI). Severity is derived from configured eval metrics (exact-match, BLEU drop, hallucination flag), mapped to a 1-5 weight. We render a heatmap matrix: rows = cohorts, cols = failure types/buckets, cell = normalized proportional score. The context-coverage score is a normalized aggregate that penalizes under-tested or high-impact cohorts. CI behavior: runs as a post-eval hook. Default is soft-fail (annotate PR and open an advisory alert) and will fail the CI only when coverage < 0.6 AND proportional failure mass > threshold for two consecutive runs. There is an opt-in strict mode in repo eval.yaml to convert soft-fails into hard blocks. Implementation summary: - New hook entry point: eval_harness/hooks/proportional_failure_heatmap.py - Cohort sampler & cache adaptor: eval_harness/samplers/contextual_cohort_sampler.py - Heatmap renderer + export: eval_harness/reporting/coverage_heatmap_v1.py - CLI/backfill helper: tools/heatmap_backfill.py - Dashboard defs: infra/dashboards/coverage-heatmap.json - Unit + integration tests: tests/hooks/test_proportional_heatmap.py + tests/samplers/test_contextual_cohort.py Backwards compatibility: hook uses existing eval outputs; no changes required to model outputs or existing prompt sets. Rollout plan: 1) Merge in soft-fail mode, enable on canary branch for 48 hours (automated job), 2) run backfill for last 30 days using tools/heatmap_backfill.py to populate dashboards, 3) after observing false positive rate < 4% and stable signal for 1 week, flip opt-in projects to strict gating. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test (CI job) - [x] Dashboard JSON added - [x] Documentation snippet added to docs/hooks.md - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-2345) - [x] Backfill tool included

review_conversation: Maya Gupta: Nice proposal. Can you clarify how frequency_factor is estimated during CI when we don't have live traffic?

Ethan Park: Good question — CI uses a sample-proxy histogram: we synthesize frequency from historical sample rates (last 7 days) stored in the eval cache. If unavailable, a conservative uniform prior is applied and flagged in the report.
Lina Sørensen: The severity mapping table looks arbitrary; please add tests that show sensitivity when weights change.
Ethan Park: Added parameterized tests and a short section in docs explaining how to tune weights per org. Tests cover weight ranges 0.5-3.0 and the coverage score stability.
Rafael Ortega: One nit — avoid expensive tensor ops in the hook path; move heavy compute to background/backfill where possible.
Ethan Park: Moved the full embedding-based clustering to the backfill tool; CI uses cached cluster ids and a cheap hash + shingle fallback. Updated implementation accordingly.
Maya Gupta: Approved after the cache optimization and tests. 👍

merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Maya Gupta. Squash commit message: feat(eval-hook): proportional failure heatmap + coverage CI hook (ENG-2345)
notes: This PR intentionally defaults to soft-fail to gather signal before blocking. Projects with high sensitivity to regression should opt into strict gating via eval.yaml. The backfill tool can be rate-limited against production traces — run with caution and on a backfill VM.
testing_instructions: Run pytests: pytest tests/hooks/test_proportional_heatmap.py::test_heatmap_aggregation and pytest tests/samplers/test_contextual_cohort.py. To simulate CI behavior locally: python -m eval_harness.hooks.proportional_failure_heatmap --input tests/fixtures/sample_eval_output.json --mode dry-run
implementation_notes: Heatmap normalization uses a per-cohort z-score with outlier trimming (winsorize 99th perc). Time decay uses exponential half-life parameter set to 7 days by default. All thresholds are configurable in eval.yaml under hooks.proportional_heatmap.
